name: Binaural Classical
description: Concert music for headphones: original pieces in classical styles that use the two ears as part of the score, each a complete movement of one and a half to nearly three minutes with its own form and a real ending. Brass choirs answering from opposite galleries, a canon whose voices enter from around your head, a nocturne over a pad that spreads from the centre to all around you, divided violins after Tchaikovsky, a chorale placed by tiny delays, an adagio whose strings drift apart in cents, an organ split by partials, a rotating chorale and a delta-wave lullaby. Each sketch explains its trick and its form in the comments. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Antiphonal Canzona
sketches.description: Venetian polychoral music: two brass choirs, one at each ear, answer each other bar by bar across a church. The left gallery intones alone, the right gallery has an echo to itself, and both join with timpani for a tutti and a broadening coda over a centred organ pedal. About a minute and a half.

sketches.name: Canon Around You
sketches.description: A three-voice canon over a D pedal: the first violin enters ahead-left, the second a bar later ahead-right, and the viola two bars later from behind you, while the cello stays in front. After a short prelude the canon is played twice, the second time as a baroque double in repeated notes, and the piece closes on a held D major chord. About a minute and three quarters.

sketches.name: Nocturne in Phase
sketches.description: A piano nocturne in E-flat sings in the centre of your head while a string pad underneath steps from in phase to 90 and 180 degrees in every section, spreading from a point into a haze around you. The song moves down to the tenor in the middle section and returns an octave higher, then everything gathers back to the centre on a final chord. Soft rain falls outside, uncorrelated in each ear. On speakers the 180-degree bars of the pad nearly vanish. About two minutes.

sketches.name: Divided Violins
sketches.description: After the finale of Tchaikovsky's Sixth Symphony: a falling melody and a rising countermelody are shared between the first violins in the left ear and the seconds in the right, swapping on every note. Each ear alone plays a jagged line; many listeners instead hear smooth lines grouped by pitch. A reveal section gives each ear the smooth line instead, so you can compare, before the divided passage returns, swells and settles on D major. About a minute and a half.

sketches.name: Chorale in Delays
sketches.description: A four-part chorale in G whose voices are placed only by tiny delays between the ears: soprano left, alto right, tenor slightly left, bass dead centre. In the second verse the voices swap sides, and in the third they all gather in the centre, with organ interludes between. An organ underneath is widened by a longer, precedence-range delay that grows bar by bar, and an unaccompanied amen closes the piece. About a minute and a half.
sketches.source:
setcpm(60/4)

// The form: an organ intonation, three verses with organ interludes between, and a sung amen
song("intonation@4 verse@4 interlude@2 verse'@4 interlude@2 verse''@4 amen@2", "once")
// The amen broadens
tempomap("0:15 20:15 22:10")

// Under about 0.7 ms a delay between the ears moves a voice sideways
// Negative values lean left, positive values lean right; the bass has no delay at all
// In the second verse the voices swap sides; in the third they all sing from the centre
soprano: note("<[g4 g4 a4 b4] [c5 b4 a4@2] [b4 c5 d5 c5] [b4 a4 g4@2]>")
  .s("ooh").itd(-.5).attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.2)
  .sections("verse").variant(x => x.itd(.5), x => x.itd(0))
alto: note("<[d4 e4 f#4 g4] [g4 g4 f#4@2] [g4 g4 g4 a4] [g4 f#4 d4@2]>")
  .s("ooh").itd(.5).attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.18)
  .sections("verse").variant(x => x.itd(-.5), x => x.itd(0))
tenor: note("<[b3 c4 d4 d4] [e4 d4 d4@2] [d4 e4 d4 e4] [d4 d4 b3@2]>")
  .s("ooh").itd(-.25).attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.18)
  .sections("verse").variant(x => x.itd(.25), x => x.itd(0))
bass: note("<[g2 c3 d3 g2] [c3 g2 d3@2] [g2 c3 b2 a2] [d3 d3 g2@2]>")
  .s("ooh").attack(.08).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.22).sections("verse")

// From about 1 to 30 ms the organ stays on the leading side but grows wider each bar
// It plays everywhere but the amen, alone in the intonation and the interludes
organ: note("<[g2,d3,g3] [c3,g3,c4] [g2,d3,b3] [d3,a3,d4]>").s("sawtooth").timbre("organ")
  .itd("<1 6 12 20>").lpf(900).attack(.4).sustain(.8).release(1).space("church").gain(.1)
  .exceptSections("amen")

// The amen, unaccompanied and centred: C to G
amen: note("<[c3,g3,e4,c5] [g2,g3,d4,b4]>").s("ooh")
  .attack(.2).release(2).room(.5).gain(.16).sections("amen")

sketches.name: Adagio in Cents
sketches.description: A slow string adagio in B-flat minor. The string orchestra's ears drift further apart in cents with each section: 2 cents beats slowly in the introduction, 6 and 12 shimmer like a larger section, and 30 blooms into a chorus at the climax, before a final chord returns to 2. The solo violin, an octave higher the second time, and the cellos stay true in the centre. About two and three quarter minutes.

sketches.name: Split Toccata
sketches.description: An organ toccata in D minor with spectral fusion: the manual's arpeggios send alternate partials to each ear, and the chords split lows from highs at 600 Hz. Neither ear hears the whole organ; together, and in mono, it sounds complete. The manual opens alone, the pedal and chords join, the toccata returns in repeated notes, and a broad D major chord ends it. About a minute and a half.

sketches.name: Rotary Chorale
sketches.description: A chorale prelude: a reed stop sings the hymn in the centre while the accompanying organ chords turn their interaural phase, once every four seconds in the prelude, every two in the first verse, twice a second in the interlude and once a second in the second verse, so the harmony rolls around inside your head. The hymn returns an octave higher, and the postlude settles on a slowly turning C major chord. All rates stay below 3 Hz. About two minutes.

sketches.name: Twilight Quartet
sketches.description: A string quartet movement in A minor in sonata shape, where nothing is panned, yet the first violin's brightness wanders between the ears: a low-pass on each ear alone sweeps in opposite directions. The development turns to C major, and in the recapitulation the sweeps swap ears. The viola is thinner on the right, where a high-pass cuts its body. About two minutes.
sketches.source:
setcpm(66/4)

// The form: a short introduction, an exposition, a development in C major, the recapitulation (exposition') and a coda
song("intro@2 exposition@8 development@8 exposition'@8 coda@4", "once")
tempomap("0:16.5 26:16.5 30:11")

// A minor everywhere, except C major in the development
const key = bysec("development:C:major *:A:minor")

// First violin: a low-pass on each ear alone, sweeping in opposite directions over each section
// The level stays put; only the brightness wanders between the ears
// In the recapitulation the two sweeps swap ears
violin: n("0 2 4 7 4 2 0 2").add("<0 0 3 3 4 4 0 0>").scale(key).transpose(12)
  .s("sawtooth").vib(5.5).vibdepth(.1)
  .lcutoff(saw.range(500, 4000).slow(8)).rcutoff(isaw.range(500, 4000).slow(8))
  .attack(.02).decay(.2).sustain(.4).release(.2).room(.4).gain(.18)
  .sections("exposition development")
  .variant(x => x.lcutoff(isaw.range(500, 4000).slow(8)).rcutoff(saw.range(500, 4000).slow(8)))

// Second violin plucks the chord tones, from the first bar to the coda
pizz: n("[0 ~ 4 ~]*2").add("<0 0 3 3 4 4 0 0>").scale(key)
  .s("triangle").timbre("bright").decay(.15).sustain(0).release(.2).room(.4).gain(.18)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// A high-pass on the right ear only: the viola sounds fuller on the left
viola: note("<[c4,e4] [c4,e4] [d4,f4] [d4,f4] [e4,g4] [e4,b4] [c4,e4] [c4,e4]>")
  .s("sawtooth").rhcutoff(1000).lpf(1600).attack(.3).sustain(.8).release(.8).room(.4).gain(.12)
  .sections("exposition")
violaDev: note("<[e4,g4] [e4,g4] [f4,a4] [f4,a4] [g4,b4] [g4,d5] [e4,g4] [e4,g4]>")
  .s("sawtooth").rhcutoff(1000).lpf(1600).attack(.3).sustain(.8).release(.8).room(.4).gain(.12)
  .sections("development")

// The cello on the roots, the same in both ears
cello: note("<a2 a2 d2 d2 e2 e2 a2 a2>").s("sawtooth").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.08)
  .lpf(700).attack(.2).sustain(.7).release(.8).room(.4).gain(.24)
  .sections("intro exposition")
celloDev: note("<c2 c2 f2 f2 g2 g2 c2 c2>").s("sawtooth").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.08)
  .lpf(700).attack(.2).sustain(.7).release(.8).room(.4).gain(.24)
  .sections("development")

// The coda: the quartet holds a last A minor chord
final: note("[a2,e3,c4,e4,a4]").slow(4).s("sawtooth").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.08)
  .lpf(1400).attack(.6).sustain(.7).release(3).room(.5).gain(.1).sections("coda")

sketches.name: Delta Lullaby
sketches.description: Headphones on: an original cradle song in 3/4 on a music box floating above your head, over a 2 Hz binaural drone in the delta range, below the rates that trigger a pulse warning. The drone begins alone, the music box sings, a voice hums the tune, the music box returns an octave higher and further away, and a last chime fades into the crickets. About a minute and a half.
